questions.prompt: What is the capital city of North Macedonia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the North Macedonia article.

questions.proof: The capital and largest city is Skopje, with more than 500,000 residents.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with North Macedonia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture North Macedonia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the North Macedonia article.

questions.proof: North Macedonia is bordered by Serbia, Albania, Greece and Bulgaria.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of North Macedonia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the North Macedonia article.

questions.proof: The language spoken by the majority of the population is Macedonian.

questions.prompt: What money is used in North Macedonia?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the North Macedonia article.

questions.proof: The country's currency is the Macedonian denar (MKD).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Ottoman Empire was originally a small city-state in _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “city-state”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Ottoman rule” part of the North Macedonia article.

questions.proof: The Ottoman Empire was originally a small city-state in Turkey.
